evaluations.prompt: which instruction in my MI300 kernel stalls the most?
expected_behavior: queries the device for supported PC sampling configurations before choosing an interval
sorts the analysis by sample count and reads the stall reason column
unexpected_behavior: hardcodes a sampling interval without querying the device

evaluations.prompt: map the hot GPU instructions back to my HIP source lines
expected_behavior: states that source line mapping requires the application to be built with debug info
notes that samples map to assembly even without debug info
unexpected_behavior: promises source line attribution for a build with no debug info

evaluations.prompt: should I use stochastic or host trap PC sampling on this GPU?
expected_behavior: explains that only stochastic records a stall reason
notes stochastic needs MI300 or newer and host_trap is the fallback
checks what the installed device actually supports

evaluations.prompt: export the annotated disassembly with sample counts from my pc sampling workload
expected_behavior: notes that the per-kernel disassembly is written under per_kernel_pc_sampling

evaluations.prompt: my host trap PC sampling run has no stall reasons, how do I interpret them?
expected_behavior: explains that host_trap records no stall reason
offers stochastic sampling if the device supports it
unexpected_behavior: interprets a stall reason from host-trap data

evaluations.note: Hotspot wording, but ranking whole kernels is counter work, not instruction sampling.
evaluations.prompt: which of my GPU kernels accounts for the most total time?
profile my C++ program's CPU hotspots with perf
do instruction level sampling on my CUDA kernel
